system_prompt_style.note: Loom runs beside a host agent (Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode); the host's system prompt is not in the evidence. Request generation code was not opened.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: Lets agents read field groups, reference profiles, task contracts, and repair context instead of repeatedly loading broad files or entire artifacts.
env_context_strategy.note: Loom routes compact context (requestReadPlan, MCP field resources) and BM25/TF-IDF knowledge retrieval (src/python/algorithms/bm25.py in the file tree). The host agent also navigates with its own tools.

context_compaction.note: Compaction is done by the host agent. Loom only survives it through .loom/ state; no compaction code is in the evidence.

observation_format.evidence_quote: The plugin routes the request to Loom tools and follows the structured next action returned by the MCP server.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: In all agents, the command starts the same Loom MCP delivery protocol.
tool_call_format.note: Loom tools are called as MCP tools through the host agent's tool calling.

tool_count.note: The MCP tool registry (Rust) was not in the evidence.

edit_primitive.note: Editing is done by the host agent's tools.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: installs the Rust MCP server, bundles the Python algorithm runtime, writes the agent MCP registration

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: Multi-agent MCP protocol | Runs the same delivery state machine through Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, and future MCP-capable agents.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: It keeps the work moving through a simple loop: plan, build, test, fix, preview, and hand off.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: Convert contracts into task plans with ownership, read groups, write boundaries, verification intent, and result templates.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: Loom is an open-source harness that runs beside the agent you already use.
multi_agent_topology.note: Multi-agent refers to multiple host agents sharing state, not a spawned topology.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: Clarify and confirm scope, optionally using registered knowledge sources.
human_in_loop.note: Manual review is also a routing target.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: Loom saves the important project state: requirements, task progress, test results, runtime facts, and repair notes.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: Scope and architecture decisions are saved and reused across sessions.
long_term_memory.note: Skills live under plugins/shared/loom/skills. Knowledge indexes are BM25/TF-IDF, not vector stores.

state_persistence.evidence_quote: Reopen the agent session and run `@loom continue` in Codex or `/loom continue` in Claude Code and OpenCode; Loom will route the next step from the saved delivery state.

self_verification.evidence_quote: Separates implementation from validation through review signals, TaskResult evidence, repair contracts, multi-target repair routing, and re-verification.
self_verification.note: Review runs as a separate step. Whether that step uses a separate model is unclear.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: Loom runs as a local MCP delivery state machine.
execution_isolation.note: Actions run in the host agent. Deploy previews use Docker Compose.

filesystem_access.note: Task write boundaries are mentioned but their enforcement is unseen.

tracing.evidence_quote: Reports, logs, previews, and repair history make the final state inspectable.

target_domain.evidence_quote: An open delivery harness that helps Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and other coding agents finish larger software tasks without losing state.

open_source.evidence_quote: Loom is open source under the [Apache License 2.0](./LICENSE).

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: Runs the same delivery state machine through Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, and future MCP-capable agents.
